executive_summary: This project will deliver an AI‑driven conversational role‑play training platform for sales associates, enabling rapid, on‑demand practice on tablets or computers. Leveraging a multi‑tenant, white‑label SaaS architecture on Microsoft Azure, the solution provides content ingestion, real‑time scoring, and manager dashboards while meeting ISO 27001 and SOC2 compliance. Key decisions include using Azure OpenAI for the LLM engine, React with TypeScript for the UI, and Azure Functions with API Management for a serverless, scalable backend. The recommendation is to proceed with the proposed Azure‑centric design, targeting a pilot MVP by end‑June and full launch before October, staying within the $500k‑$800k budget.
background_summary: The client currently conducts sales training manually, relying on a single trainer to manage 135 accounts, resulting in inconsistent role‑playing experiences and limited visibility into training effectiveness. There is no integration with the POS system, and the organization seeks a low‑cost, AI‑enabled solution that can be quickly piloted and later expanded across multiple partner accounts.

functional_requirements.requirement: The platform must provide AI‑driven conversational role‑play simulations for sales associates.
Users must be able to upload training content such as brochures, PowerPoint decks, and pitch scripts for the AI to learn from.
The system must generate real‑time scoring and feedback on associate performance.
Managers need a dashboard to view practice frequency, scores, attach‑rate uplift, and individual associate transcripts.
The solution must support difficulty levels and objection‑handling scenarios.
A transcript of each role‑play interaction must be stored and accessible for review.
The MVP must operate as a separate tool without POS integration, using manual comparison for effectiveness.
The platform must be white‑labelable so the client can retain IP and resale it to other partners.
The solution should be duplicable for multiple partner accounts (e.g., Assurant, Amazon, Samsung).
Support basic multimodal input (voice via ElevenLabs, text) for the MVP, with future expansion to audio/video.
The system must be able to run on tablets or computers during short lull periods (3–5 minutes per associate).
Provide a scoring engine that can be tuned by managers to ensure AI evaluation aligns with expert judgment.
Generate reports that correlate associate practice data with ESP attach‑rate metrics.
The platform must be hosted on a cloud environment (preferably Azure) and take advantage of hyperscaler funding programs where possible.
Deliver a proof‑of‑concept with defined KPIs (attach‑rate uplift, practice frequency, score improvement).

non_functional_requirements.requirement: System must respond to user interactions within 2 seconds for text and 3 seconds for voice synthesis.
Comply with ISO 27001 and SOC2; all secrets stored in Azure Key Vault; data encrypted at rest and in transit.
Architecture must handle bursty training sessions from multiple tenants, scaling automatically via Azure Functions and Cosmos DB.
Achieve 99.9% uptime across all services using Azure regional redundancy and health monitoring.
Infrastructure defined as code (Bicep) to enable repeatable tenant provisioning and easy updates.

risk_assessment.impact: High – core conversational capability may be unavailable or too expensive for pilot scale.
risk_assessment.mitigation_strategy: Start with pre‑trained GPT‑4o mini model without fine‑tuning for the pilot, and validate cost using Azure cost calculators; defer custom fine‑tuning to post‑pilot phase.

risk_assessment.risk: Multi‑tenant data isolation using Cosmos DB containers and AD B2C claims can become complex to manage at scale, risking data leakage between partners.
risk_assessment.impact: Medium – violates IP protection and compliance requirements.
risk_assessment.mitigation_strategy: Implement automated Bicep scripts that create a dedicated Cosmos DB database per tenant and enforce strict Azure Policy checks; conduct penetration testing before launch.

risk_assessment.risk: Power BI Embedded licensing and per‑tenant workspace provisioning may inflate operational costs and extend the timeline for dashboard rollout.
risk_assessment.impact: Medium – manager dashboards could be delayed, reducing proof‑of‑concept KPI visibility.

risk_assessment.risk: Dependency on external ElevenLabs API for voice synthesis introduces third‑party availability and latency risks.
risk_assessment.impact: Low to Medium – voice output quality is a key feature but can fallback to text‑only.

recommendations_next_steps: Immediately initiate Azure subscription validation, set up the Azure AD B2C tenant, and spin up a pilot environment using the Bicep IaC scripts. Assemble a cross‑functional delivery team (product owner, AI specialist, front‑end, back‑end, DevOps, security). Follow an MVP‑first approach: deliver core role‑play, content upload, real‑time scoring, and a lightweight manager view by end‑June. Parallelly run cost‑modeling for Azure OpenAI usage and negotiate Power BI licensing. After pilot validation, iterate to add fine‑tuned LLMs, expanded multimodal input, and full Power BI dashboards, outlining a roadmap for Q4 rollout and subsequent partner onboarding.
architecture_summary: The chosen Azure‑centric, serverless multi‑tenant SaaS architecture meets the client’s need for rapid deployment, cost efficiency, and strict compliance. Azure AD B2C provides secure, white‑label authentication, and Power BI Embedded delivers per‑tenant analytics. This design aligns with business goals of low upfront investment, quick time‑to‑value, and the ability to duplicate the platform for multiple partners.

architecture_summary.overview: A serverless, multi‑tenant SaaS hosted on Azure that delivers AI‑driven role‑play simulations via a React web app. Content is ingested, indexed, and served to an LLM (Azure OpenAI) which interacts with users through text or ElevenLabs voice. A scoring microservice evaluates performance in real time, storing transcripts and scores in Cosmos DB. Managers view analytics through Power BI Embedded dashboards. Azure AD B2C handles tenant‑aware authentication and white‑label branding.
architecture_summary.workflow: 1. Associate accesses the React UI (static web app). 2. UI calls Azure API Management which routes to tenant‑specific Azure Functions. 3. Functions invoke Azure OpenAI for conversational response and ElevenLabs for voice output. 4. Interaction transcript is sent to the scoring function, which applies configurable rules and returns a real‑time score. 5. Transcript and score are persisted in Cosmos DB and Blob Storage. 6. Power BI pulls data per tenant for manager dashboards and exportable reports.
architecture_summary.data_flow: Upload → Form Recognizer → Cognitive Search index → Azure OpenAI prompts → Conversation → Scoring Function → Cosmos DB (transcript/score) + Blob (raw audio) → Power BI → Manager dashboard.
